area: Input buffering vs the OG's measured semantics (busy-state gating, deferred strokes, after-attack window)

items.title: Generic fixed-window input buffer (5–15 frames / 80–250 ms) as the stroke mechanism
items.claim: Canon practice (fighting games and action games alike) stores an input pressed during recovery in a short fixed window — typically 5–15 frames (~80–250 ms); Smash Bros uses 9–10 frames, SFV 3, GBVSR extends to 6–7 on wake-up — executes it on the first actionable frame, and silently discards it if the window expires. Applying this to SSHD strokes (e.g. 'a 120ms buffer') would be a fidelity DEFECT twice over: the OG outright REJECTS a stroke drawn during hit-recovery (it vanishes after 1 content tick, no dash, no damage — never buffered), and it DEFERS a busy-state stroke for up to ~1.4 s (~21 content ticks ≈ 84 sim frames), an order of magnitude past any canon window, keeping it visibly rendered the whole time.

sources.title: Input Buffering for Better Combat Responsiveness

items.adjudication_reason: Contradicts ledger §S24-A.6 row K1 (hit-recovery stroke vanishes after 1 tick — a buffer would execute it) and the PENDING row Honda f0116–f0138 (~1.4 s deferral — a 120–250 ms window would expire it). Sim.applyStroke today has NEITHER behavior: it executes every manual stroke immediately regardless of playerBusyUntilFrame, so the fix is the OG spec in the next item, not a canon buffer.
items.implementation_note: Guidance for A12.2: do not add any *_BUFFER_MS constant to src/config/. The OG's semantics are state-conditional (reject vs defer), not time-window.

items.title: OG-faithful spec: busy-state gating + single-slot deferred-stroke queue in Sim, blink rendered by the scene
items.claim: The one piece of canon that DOES match the OG is 'buffered input executes on the first actionable frame after recovery' (SmashWiki; salivity). Spec: (1) add a hit-recovery state to FighterState — hitRecoveryUntilFrame set in dealDamage when the player is the target, seeded from §S24-E/F measurements (mid-combo hit hold 4–5 content ticks = 16–20 sim frames; knockdown ~6 ticks; global hit-stop 3 ticks), since Sim currently flags 'Stun is NOT modelled'. (2) In applyStroke (manual source): if frameCount < hitRecoveryUntilFrame → REJECT: no dash, no damage, emit a strokeRejected event so DuelScene draws the 1-tick vanish (K1). (3) Else if frameCount < playerBusyUntilFrame (already computed from SLASH_FRAMES windup+active+recovery, today gating only AUTO SLASH) → DEFER: store the DrawnStroke in a single pendingStroke slot, emit strokePending; in tick(), on the first frame past busy, run it through the same applyStroke slash path. (4) No expiry timer — the OG's ~1.4 s is 'until recovery', not a window; clear on fight end. (5) Render: scene draws the pending polyline blinking 3-on/1–2-off content ticks (4 sim frames per content tick), phase derived from Sim.frame via the pending events — scene stays render-only.

sources.title: Input Buffering for Better Combat Responsiveness
The Art of Input Buffering — Wayline

items.adjudication_reason: Directly implements ledger §S24-C's build consequence ('K1-rejection + PENDING-blink rows give the busy-state gating') on existing seams: Sim.playerBusyUntilFrame and SLASH_FRAMES already exist, applyStroke is the single entry point both manual and auto strokes take (D7), and SimEvent is the established scene channel — no new architecture needed.
items.implementation_note: Constants to add in src/config/: HIT_RECOVERY_FRAMES (CONTRACT — §S24-E 4–5 ticks), STROKE_REJECT_VANISH_TICKS=1 (CONTRACT — K1), PENDING_BLINK_ON/OFF ticks (CONTRACT — §S24-A.6). Chaos-test both gates: plant a stroke inside hit-recovery (must reject), inside own-swing (must defer then execute), and verify the pre-A12.2 behavior (immediate execution) goes red.

items.title: Song's 'After Attack Delay' (Game Developer, 2005) — the canon rationale for DEFER-not-drop during own-swing recovery
items.claim: Jiesang Song (main game programmer, Kingdom Under Fire: The Crusaders) documents the technique the orchestrator asked about: after an attack, the character animation lingers so the player's next attack input is accepted even when the button press missed the precise timing — Devil May Cry, PoP: Warrior Within, and Ninja Gaiden all do it, purely as an input-responsiveness device. This is exactly the design intent behind the OG's PENDING behavior (a busy-state stroke waits and then chains), and §S24-E's 'chained strike = 0–1 tick' landing hold confirms the chain comes out essentially on the first free tick.

sources.title: Improving the Combat 'Impact' Of Action Games — Jiesang Song, Game Developer 2005

items.adjudication_reason: The principle (accept the late input, execute at recovery end) survives verbatim, but the parameterization must come from the ledger, not Song: acceptance window = the whole playerBusyUntilFrame period (§S24-A.6 PENDING shows ~1.4 s, not a lingering-animation fudge), execution beat from SLASH_FRAMES (src/config/timing.ts) + §S24-E landing holds, and — unlike every canon implementation — the deferred stroke stays VISIBLE, blinking. Fully subsumed by the item-2 spec; listed separately because it is the requested canon anchor.
items.implementation_note: Already excerpted in docs/research/2026-08-05-improvements-research.md (rows 129/364/573) — cross-link the A12.2 commit to it.

items.title: Reject/defer boundary, pending-slot replacement policy, and deferral timeout are underdetermined — measure before pinning CONTRACT
items.claim: The ledger has exactly two data points: K1 (rejected — drawn 1 tick after a hit flash, mid-slide, left end 29 px behind center) and PENDING (deferred ~1.4 s). Three unknowns a wrong guess would fossilize: (a) is the boundary hit-recovery-vs-own-swing, or early-vs-late recovery (canon precedent for the latter: GBVSR widens the buffer specifically on wake-up; Brawl forbids buffering out of tumble hitstun entirely — state-dependent rules are normal)? (b) if a second stroke is drawn while one is pending, does it replace the slot (canon: newer input wins — Yosi Spring; Smash's priority hierarchy) or get ignored? (c) does deferral ever time out, or only resolve at recovery/fight-end? Scan both longplays for double-stroke-while-busy and late-recovery-stroke instances before tagging these CONTRACT.

items.title: Residual use of generic-canon numbers: INFERRED seeds and latency sanity bands only
items.claim: Canon buffer numbers keep three narrow jobs here: (1) the 80–250 ms canon band and Celeste's few-frame jump buffer (Thorson: press-before-landing executes on the landing frame) bracket the OG's own 66.7 ms content-tick quantization — a sanity bound that scene pointer-up → applyStroke commit latency must stay within ~1 content tick, or K1-vs-K2-class distinctions (2 ticks apart) become irreproducible; (2) if the SESSION 25 measurement finds late-hit-recovery strokes deferring rather than rejecting, GBVSR's 6–7-frame wake-up buffer is the right INFERRED seed for that sliver; (3) Yosi Spring's consumed-input clearing (clear the slot on execution so one stroke can never double-fire) is a correctness pattern for the pendingStroke slot regardless of parameters. Everything else about canon buffers has no purchase on this game.

dead_ends: "Song's after-attack delay" was ungoogleable as a fighting-game or CHI term (searches for Song + after-attack delay + input study returned only music/adaptive-audio papers); it resolved via repo grep to Jiesang Song's 2005 Game Developer article, already excerpted in docs/research/2026-08-05-improvements-research.md, and the live URL was then confirmed by fetch. grokipedia.com/page/Input_buffer_fighting_games returned HTTP 403; glossary.infil.net is JS-rendered and returned no content via fetch (its 'Delay Tech' entry URL from search results was therefore not used as a source). No canon source anywhere discusses VISUAL feedback for a buffered/pending input — the OG's blinking pending stroke has no canon analogue, so its render spec rests entirely on ledger §S24-A.6.
